crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Thematic Coding
children.blurb: Thematic coding is a core method in qualitative analysis for identifying, analyzing, and reporting patterns, or themes, within textual data such as interview transcripts, open-ended survey responses, and field notes.

children.name: Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation
children.blurb: Interview transcription and speaker separation covers the conversion of recorded interviews into written text and the labelling of who spoke when.

children.name: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
children.blurb: Finding patterns in lived experience is a qualitative and mixed methods research activity.

children.name: Ethnographic Synthesis
children.blurb: Ethnographic synthesis is the work of drawing together findings from two or more ethnographic or closely observational studies into a single comparative account.

children.name: Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data
children.blurb: Combining qualitative and quantitative data, often called mixed methods, is the practice of bringing narrative, observational, or interview material together with counts, measurements, or statistical summaries in one study.

sections.body: Qualitative analysis and mixed methods cover the work of turning interviews, field notes, and open ended responses into findings that can be compared and combined with numbers. In practice, AI is used to transcribe recorded interviews, separate speakers, suggest first pass codes, and cluster passages that seem to share a theme. Researchers still read the material, but the machine handles the sorting and retrieval that used to consume weeks. The output is not a conclusion, it is a set of candidate patterns that a person then checks against the transcripts. This is one of the areas where AI assists most and decides least.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Transcription is largely solved for clear audio in common languages, though accents, overlapping speech, and noisy field recordings still produce errors that need correction. Thematic coding is partly solved at the level of suggestion, and not solved at the level of interpretation, because a model can group similar sentences but cannot know what a passage means to the person who said it. Pattern finding across lived experience is the weakest area, since models tend to flatten contradiction and outlier cases that often carry the most information. Ethnographic synthesis resists automation because it depends on long immersion and context that never appears in the text. Mixed methods work is procedurally supported but conceptually unresolved, and no tool removes the judgment call about how to weight a theme against a statistic. The honest limit is that these systems produce plausible summaries, and plausible is not the same as correct.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The section moves from raw material to interpretation to integration. Thematic Coding is the entry point for anyone who needs to understand how a codebook is built and where a model can help propose labels. Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation sits underneath it, covering the conversion of audio into text and the attribution of who said what. Finding Patterns in Lived Experience takes the coded material and asks what recurs across participants, which is where the gap between frequency and meaning becomes visible. Ethnographic Synthesis addresses the longer form work of making sense of a field site or a community over time, and it is the page to read when the data is observational rather than interview based. Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data closes the section by treating the join between themes and measurements, which is the point where most mixed methods projects either hold together or fall apart.
